utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, The Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm sorry for the delay this morning. We lost almost an hour, so it is impossible for us to make it up. So this morning, we will only have two sittings. We'll break at 11.30, and after the break we will continue. I hope such kind of delay will never happen again. Well, Mr. McCloskey, are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Good morning. We are ready to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. McCloskey: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We left off on the evening of 11 July. You had ended by telling us that you had told Colonel Jankovic of the able-bodied Muslim men in Potocari. Where were you when you informed Colonel Jankovic of this information?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, 1995, in the evening, I was in my office at the brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there any other discussion on any other related matters after you informed him of that, that you recall?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Colonel Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In connection with Colonel Jankovic, yes. As for that day, and the intelligence I received on that day, I told Colonel Jankovic whatever I found out through intelligence organs from the units, from the Bratunac Brigade, the battalion. And especially, I conveyed to him the information I received from the 2nd Infantry Battalion. After that, we talked about the duties we were facing and the meeting that was scheduled for 11.00 the same evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, there is a buzz in my ear after he finishes talking. Maybe I can switch... That sounds...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is that okay now? If not, we'll have the technician come in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't hear it any more, Your Honour. If I start hearing buzzes, I'll let you know. But it's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, could you outline just briefly the intelligence situation that you informed Colonel Jankovic that night, that you were getting from the battalions.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, briefly. During the day, I was receiving information from the intelligence organ of the 2nd infantry battalion, information on the movement from Srebrenica towards the U.N. Base, DutchBat base in Potocari. I was told that there were large numbers of people moving down that road. Later, it turned out that those had been civilians. On the basis of their reports and their assessment, we found out that there had been able-bodied men among those people. And my information was among those people moving towards the town, there were between 1.000 and 2.000 able-bodied military age men. For the most part, I received this information personally from the intelligence and security organ. Later, when I talked to people in the operations room, when I talked to the operations duty officer, I found out that the operations duty officer at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters was receiving the same information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any information about the 28th division forces that evening?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That evening, there was some indications, some assessments that forces of the 28th division had abandoned the town of Srebrenica. And that they headed for the Jaglici and Susnjari village areas. They headed towards an area where there was a passage that they had used before during the war. Those units were grouping, forces were being evacuated to head for those villages, or rather, areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you share that information with Colonel Jankovic also?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did share that with him. Colonel Jankovic, as I said, was staying in my office the whole time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mention that had you spoke to Colonel Jankovic about the upcoming second meeting of 11 July. What did you discuss with him about that next meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We only agreed very briefly what to do. Rather, that we should continue the tasks that I had started, that we should carrying out preparations for the meeting that was scheduled for 2300 hours, that was expected to take place at 2300 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were those preparations?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly those were regular preparations concerning security measures that would be taken in cases where officers from the main staff or from the corps command were in the area, providing security for the Fontana Hotel where the meeting was scheduled to take place. It was about providing physical security and taking other measures related to security measures and making sure that representatives of DutchBat and the Muslim side got there safely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the brigade command at about this time, did you speak about any of these matters to your commander, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, in that period, in the evening on the 11th, I did not personally see Commander Blagojevic. But I've said in my previous testimony that whatever information I had on enemy forces and activities, and whatever other information I had, I duly informed the duty operations officer about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from the duty operations officer, did you speak to any other Bratunac Brigade officers that night, before going back -- or before leaving the office?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, it was Colonel Jankovic. I can't remember specifically whether I talked to him about those tasks, except the talks that I had with the military police commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, aside from what you've told us earlier, did you have any additional talks with the military police commander, who is, as you have stated, Mirko Jankovic, just so we're not confused, not Colonel Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the military police commander, I told him that some of his military policemen would again be needed at 11.00 to provide security at the Fontana Hotel during the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was the next thing you did after these discussions with Colonel Jankovic and Mirko Jankovic? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went myself to the Fontana Hotel, and I was preparing the security measure, the carrying out of the security measures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe for us that meeting, who was there, who did you see arrive at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That evening, at the second meeting, I saw General Ratko Mladic, commander of the main staff. I saw General Krstic, who was the commander of the Drina Corps. I saw Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric. I saw Colonel Jankovic. They were representing the army of Republika Srpska. As for DutchBat, the commander of DutchBat, Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans was there, alongside with his deputy Major Boering, and I think Mr. Rutten, one of the other officers, was also there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a representative of the Muslims that you recall?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. I forgot about that. Representative of the Muslim side was there that evening, Mr. Nesib Mandzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to review the video of that meeting in the possession of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, you cannot be seen on that video, can you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't. During the meeting itself, I was not in the room where the meeting took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you during the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was outside that room in another room, a bigger room from which you entered the room in which the meeting was taking place. I was near the door which separated the two rooms. There is a sliding door separating the two rooms, so I was outside the room where the meeting was taking place in the other room, the bigger room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see what was going on in the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could both see and hear what was happening inside the room, who was in attendance and what was being discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your impressions of what was going on in this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may object to the line of the questioning or the way it's phrased. If he could ask the gentleman to describe what he saw, then the Court can conclude what impressions he might have formed at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. McCloskey, I could not understand your question, so maybe you could rephrase it to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe briefly what happened at the meeting, that you saw and heard.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The meeting kicked off around 11.00 as ordered by General Mladic when the DutchBat people had finished their first meeting. I already said who was present at the first meeting. And unlike the first meeting, when those present did not even sit down around the table to talk, the second meeting was more like a meeting in its nature. The first part of the meeting took place in a more or less fair atmosphere. Mr. Karremans was talking about the situation in Potocari. He was talking about priorities, in terms of what needed doing to put the situation back in control. Mr. Karremans enumerated, or rather listed, everything that he thought was urgent in Srebrenica. Mostly he was referring to medicine, to food, water, the evacuation of the wounded, assisting the wounded, supplying some of the medicines, and other issues of more or less humanitarian character. The next part of the meeting was very different in tone. General Mladic spoke to Nesib Mandzic telling him that the fate of the Muslim people was in his hands. He still insisted at the meeting that members of the civilian bodies, bodies of the civilian government and of the army, should be present at the next meeting. At one point, General Mladic said that his people could either survive or disappear and that it was all up to Mandzic, or rather down to how the situation would evolve over the next period. After that, there was nothing else worth pointing out, I think. The meeting was over. General Mladic personally ordered me to see members of DutchBat and the Muslim representatives back to the yellow bridge, Zuti Most, and back to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if anything, was anticipated for the next day based on what you saw at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Towards the end of the meeting, General Mladic said that he would order his troops to cease-fire until 10.00 the following day and that he would expect to see all of them at 10.00 attending the meeting the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you escort Mr. Mandzic and the Dutch back to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I escorted Mr. Mandzic and the Dutch as far as the yellow bridge, and then they continued on to Potocari, their base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, I went back to the yellow bridge. I told the police and members of the Bratunac Brigade who were manning the yellow bridge to take over the representatives of DutchBat the next day, that a meeting was scheduled for 10.00. And if they were no longer on duty the next day, that they should inform the people who came to relieve them about this. Then I went to the brigade headquarters. There was nothing special happening. It was already quite late, so I went back home to sleep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went back to the brigade headquarters, did you see any of the senior officers of the brigade or the corps or the main staff or any others?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, once I was back, I didn't see anyone. It was quite late in the evening. There was no one around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going on to the 12th of July, when did you come on duty on 12 July?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, I arrived just past 7.00. I came to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, to the operations room. After that, I went to my office, so that must have been just past 7.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened of significant at the Bratunac Brigade that morning, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, nothing special, nothing significant. Intelligence kept coming in from the field that the position of the Muslim convoy travelling towards Konjevic Polje and on to Cerska was already known on the 12th. This was the information that had been forwarded to us before the 12th, the morning hours on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall any meetings of senior officers at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters that morning of 12 July?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were meetings being held in that period of time at the Bratunac Brigade. But I'm still not sure whether it was on the 12th on the 13th, and I can't say specifically. I know there were a number of such meetings. However, if it was on the 12th or the 13th, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember a morning meeting on the 12th or the 13th, you're just not sure which day it is?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may object here for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The gentleman has indicated that there were "meetings" plural. And he mentioned several days. I would ask the Prosecutor to please not re-characterise the witness's testimony in a way that suggests a potential option from which the witness can select. In other words, leading the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may put it another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I will try, Mr. President. But to call the Court's attention to the answer to the witness: "But I'm still not sure whether it was on the 12th or the 13th." That's what I meant to get to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the problem is the witness said there are a number of meetings. And your question is a morning meeting on the 12th or 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that there was a number of meetings, and you also mentioned that you couldn't remember whether it was the 12th or 13th. Do you remember anything about any meetings during that time period, and if you could tell us which time period it is, to clarify?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that there were meetings on both the 12th and the 13th at the Bratunac Brigade command. But what I wish to say is that it was seven or eight years ago, and I have been reminded by certain documents that I had in my possession. So I can say that on that basis as well, I can confirm that there was a meeting on the 12th in the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there one document in particular that helps you remember a meeting on the morning of the 12th at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a document of the chief of the state security centre, Colonel Vasic which shows that in Bratunac, that meeting was held at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection -- sorry. First of all, were you at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection of who you saw present at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters at that time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't mean to interrupt the Prosecutor. However, he has made reference to a particular document. I think at this point in time, the document should be introduced or shown to the particular witness so we know exactly which document he's making reference to because the gentleman did indicate that now his memory, at least in the preparation of his direct examination, and perhaps cross, has been refreshed by documents furnished to him by his lawyers during the course of the last year or so. So he's not testifying from an independent memory, but rather from documents that he's reviewed. He has also indicated that he wasn't present at the meeting, and so at this point, I think, to make -- so we can have a clear record and for the purposes of perhaps cross-examination, the Prosecutor should show the document to the gentleman so we are sure which document in particular he's referring to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Karnavas. I believe that the Prosecutor will come to that document later. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, there -- as one might imagine, this witness as well as other witnesses have referred to many, many documents. I can't be prepared to have each document that this witness has used to refresh his recollection. That particular document is a well-known document. I can put my finger on it. It was provided to Defence counsel a few days ago. It's a well-known document. And we have it and we will tie it up. I have saved the document presentation until the end so we could hear just from the witness. And so if -- I think we can tie that document or anything else that appears relevant from the direct at the end, that which was my intention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- For the moment, I am satisfied with that answer, Your Honour. But only for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We will see. You may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you recall any senior officers present at the brigade headquarters about the time this meeting was going on?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember, Mr. McCloskey. On that day, that is, the 12th, General Mladic was present, General Krstic, Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic, Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric, and of course it was normal that Colonel Jankovic would be at the brigade headquarters. And as far as I can recollect, Mr. Or Colonel Vasic was also present from the security centre in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to, again, clear up the record, did you say Lieutenant-colonel Kosoric was present, not Osoric?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing your commander Blagojevic at the brigade headquarters that morning on 12 July?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him. He was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do that morning, 12 July?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, on the 12th of July, the talks were continued at the Fontana Hotel. And after just briefly being at the headquarters, I went to the Fontana Hotel, and I was working on the preparations for that meeting scheduled for 10.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may interrupt for one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, I could not see you because of the angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Your Honour. The previous line of questioning, the Prosecutor asked who was at the brigade headquarters, and the gentleman listed several officers. Prior to that, the gentleman talked about a meeting. Then the next question -- then shortly thereafter, he was asked whether Colonel Blagojevic was there. That is giving the impression that somehow Mr. Blagojevic was at a particular meeting that was being held. And I'm quite concerned that there's no clear record here as to whether this gentleman here saw Mr. Blagojevic on that particular morning at that particular meeting, but the transcript and the way that the presentation is going from the question and answer would somehow give the impression that since he saw him and since there were others there and since there was a meeting, somehow assuming there was a meeting that Mr. Blagojevic was also at the meeting with all these other high-powered officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey, you may ask some questions to clarify that point. From the transcript, there may be some misunderstandings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no indication that this witness saw Mr. Blagojevic at this meeting. All I know is that he was at the brigade headquarters. That's all we brought out on direct. That's what the record reflects. I can try to clear that up, but I know Mr. Karnavas is very good at cross-examination, and I will try to make that clear, clearer for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, did you ever see anyone actually at a meeting on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. McCloskey. I said that I wasn't at that meeting, and I couldn't see who was actually present at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the people that you have described present that morning at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters were the people you've already described. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whether or not they were at that meeting, you don't know because you weren't at that meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Clearly so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, is there anything else that the Court is concerned with on that point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to the Hotel Fontana, did you meet with any officers at that time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 12th, in the morning, I had a meeting prior to that meeting with Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric and Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was this that you met with them?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We met at the plateau in front of the Fontana Hotel, in front of the entrance, the plateau in front of the entrance to the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anyone else in the area of this area in the front of the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area in front of the Fontana Hotel were also members of the physical security, that is, members of the Bratunac police who came to provide security for the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if anything, was said between you and Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic and Kosoric that morning in front of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we talked. And in answer to my question to Popovic and Kosoric as to what would happen next, Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic told me that on that day, the women and children would be evacuated and that they would be evacuated in the direction of Kladanj. Also that on that day, the men, the able-bodied men, would be separated and that those men would be temporarily detained once they had been separated. And when I asked what would happen to them next, he told me that all balijas needed to be killed. That was a conversation in the presence of Popovic, myself, and Kosoric. In continuation, we discussed the provisional places of detention for the separated men. I suggested to Popovic and Kosoric that the buildings of the Vuk Karadzic elementary school, that the Djuro Pucar Stari secondary school in Bratunac, the gym, and the hangar should be used as detention facilities for the men separated from the group at Potocari. That was a part of the conversation we had. Another part of that conversation relating this operation had to do with my own role, and I was told that my task in that operation would be to coordinate the forces that would be engaged in Potocari for this operation of separation, temporary detention, and later the killing of those men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there -- were there any locations discussed for the killing of the Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Prosecutor. The places of execution were discussed, and two locations were mentioned. The first to be mentioned was the brickworks, the Ciglana, a state-owned company in Bratunac, and the area of the Sase mine in Sase village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who brought up these two locations as possible locations for execution?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned both locations. But in view of the way in which they reacted, my conclusion was that they already knew, that is, that both of them already knew about both locations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic was saying these things to you. Did Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric say anything during this discussion?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic spoke, after which the same was repeated by Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Popovic said that all the balijas needed to be killed, can you tell us what this term "balija" is a reference to and what it means?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Balija is a term mainly used to denote Muslims, so the reference was to Muslims who were at the time located in Potocari. Actually, balija is a derogatory term for the Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did this discussion between you three last roughly?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very brief. Seven to ten minutes on the outside, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do after this discussion?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that discussion, I remained in front of the Fontana Hotel. Actually, I was first at the reception desk, then within the hotel compound as I was expecting that third meeting at 10.00 to take place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did superior officers arrive at the meeting at about that time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. I can list the participants at that meeting because I saw them in person as they arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if General Mladic was present at the Hotel Fontana before or during the discussion you had with Kosoric and Popovic, or did he arrive afterward?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic was already in the Fontana Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Same question for General Krstic; do you know where he was at the time you were having this discussion with Popovic and Kosoric?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were already all of them in the Fontana before I had this conversation with Popovic and Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us from your knowledge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The gentleman indicated that "all of them." Who is "all of them" that he's now referring to? Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may ask some questions to clarify this point. I guess it's the participants of that meeting, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, that was, of course, my next question, and the interruption from counsel is I believe at this point really uncalled for. And I'm endeavouring to make this as clear as possible. It's hard when the rhythm and the flow of the question/answer is constantly broken up, but I will continue to try.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us from your own personal knowledge, besides Mladic and Krstic, who was at that Hotel Fontana meeting on the morning of the 12th?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't mean to interrupt Mr. McCloskey, but there seems to be two meetings. There's the 10.00 meeting that the gentleman said he went there to make sure that security was there and to prepare for that particular meeting. Then there was a line of questioning where he was asked was General Mladic there already. He had indicated yes. General Krstic. And then he says "all of them." So there would appear at least to be another meeting preceding the 10.00 meeting which is separate and apart from any other meeting that might have taken place at the headquarters that he might have viewed sometime between 7.00 and 9.00. So the purpose of my objection was whether when he says "all of them" is he referring to a meeting prior to the 10.00 meeting, or is it the 10.00 meeting? And I apologise if I'm interrupting or throwing off the Prosecutor. That's not my intention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I believe that you made things more complicated for us. And I'm a little bit confused about all those meetings. But anyway, this is important testimony, and we have to make that matter clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the meeting at the Hotel Fontana on the morning of the 12th that is on video. That was the main reason for you being there, according to your testimony. Again, who were you able to see that was present at that meeting on 12 July at the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, at 10.00, the meeting was attended or the people who arrived to attend that meeting were the following officers: General Mladic was present, General Krstic, Colonel Jankovic, Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric, and Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic. From the ministry of internal affairs, Colonel Vasic was present as chief of the security centre in Zvornik as well as representatives of the Dutch Battalion, Mr. Karremans, Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans, Mr. Boering, and Mr. Rutten. And from the Muslim side, the meeting was attended by Nesib Mandzic, Mr. Nuhanovic, and a lady whose name I am really unable to remember just now, a lady who was in the team representing the Muslim side. And of course, an interpreter, Petar Uscumlic, was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall an Ibro Nuhanovic being present as well?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said Ibro Nuhanovic was present as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about anyone from the civilian authorities of the Bratunac or Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, attending the meeting was the president of the Municipal Assembly of Bratunac, Ljubisav Simic; the president of the executive council of Bratunac Municipality, Srbislav Davidovic; and in the capacity of commissioner for civilian affairs of Srebrenica, Mr. Miroslav Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is this commissioner of civilian affairs that Mr. Deronjic was holding?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was nominated by the president of the republic, Mr. Karadzic, as a person who should take all necessary measures to ensure protection for the civilian population, to communicate with them, to provide medical aid, and to make sure that everything functioned in accordance with the Geneva Conventions. That is my understanding of his role. His role also was to organise the functioning of authority in Srebrenica, to appoint the chief of the MUP and the other necessary bodies for Srebrenica to renew or normalise life again. That's as much as I know regarding his role.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend this 10.00 Hotel Fontana meeting yourself?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. McCloskey, I did not attend this meeting. I was not even inside the premises where the meeting was being held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why was that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the reasons, there are several reasons. One of the reasons is that I realised fully what was going to happen, so there was absolutely no need for me to listen to what was being said. And it was my assessment that all that remained was purely technical matters on technical aspects of that operation, that is the operation of evacuation and forcible resettlement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what in your mind was going to happen at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, roughly speaking, that the demands and questions that had been discussed at the previous meeting, that is, the one held on the 12th at 2300 hours would be specified regarding provision of fuel, transportation, the provision of buses and trucks, and other such technical matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you during the time of this -- the 10.00 meeting at the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while, I was sitting in the lobby outside the hall. And a part of the time, I was in the area in front of the Fontana Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you go to Potocari and begin the responsibilities that had been discussed between you and Popovic and Kosoric?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simply because I hadn't received any specific order for a specific assignment. We did discuss these things, but it was not a concrete or specific assignment. Furthermore, the evacuation and what we had been discussed was not possible just then because there were no buses or trucks or anything like that yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that discussion with Kosoric and Popovic, were the Muslims going to be given an option to stay if they chose?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only say what my impression was, based on what I had heard. In theory, this would have been possible. In practical terms, my conclusion was that it would have been impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you base your conclusion on?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, I base the first part of my conclusion on General Mladic's statements. I will try and paraphrase what he actually said. He said that he was the one who could guarantee safety, the safety of other people, that civilians were not the target of the army of Republika Srpska, the UNPROFOR, or other members of international organisations. He said that whoever wished to stay should speak out and say so on an individual basis, whether they wanted to stay or leave. That's what he said. In theory, some of the Muslims would be allowed to stay. In practical terms, I know what Mr. Popovic and Kosoric told me. Quite simply, the position was that all civilians would be evacuated, that the men would be detained -- separated, detained, and killed. This was a position that clearly indicated the operation would go through to the very end and would be applied to everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To try to clarify this, when you say you heard General Mladic making these statements, where was it -- where was he and when did he make these statements?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was at the second meeting, at the second meeting at 11.00 when he spoke about what I've just said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the evening of 11 July?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the evening of 11th of July, 11.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you receive clear information or instructions on what you should be doing that morning of 12 July?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I received clear instructions after the meeting on the 12th of July, after the meeting that begin at 10.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did you receive those instructions from?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received those instructions once the meeting was over from Colonel Jankovic who had been present at that meeting. So following the meeting, I received instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you and Colonel Jankovic when you received instructions from him?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was outside the Fontana Hotel, and Colonel Jankovic had left the meeting. We met just after he left the Fontana Hotel, and he issued me with instructions as to what I should do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time he issued you these instructions, was there anyone else present or within earshot of you and Colonel Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that specific time, no. There were other people leaving the building. There were some policemen nearby. Two of us talked to one side, and the other people were leaving on the other side. So it wasn't possible for anyone to overhear our conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he say to you? What did Colonel Jankovic say to you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Jankovic told me what my next assignment would be. He said on the 12th, I should work in Potocari and coordinate the activities that were underway in Potocari itself, that I should give instructions and that I should coordinate the evacuation of the civilian population, of the women and children, to coordinate work on the separation of men and their temporary transfer and detention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion with Colonel Jankovic relating to the killing of the Muslim men that would be separated?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. McCloskey. There was no discussion with Colonel Jankovic about that operation, the killing of men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after receiving these instructions?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I waited for a while. I did not leave for Potocari immediately because the buses had not yet arrived at the time when I received my instructions from Colonel Jankovic. I said for a while outside the hotel in the area just in front of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Colonel Jankovic refer you to any particular person to conduct these duties with in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told me that as for coordinating those activities that were part of the operation, I should speak to Mr. Jevic who was a member of the special brigades of the MUP, Dusko Jevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who Dusko Jevic was at the time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew Dusko Jevic personally. I'd known him from before the operation. But at that time, I didn't know precisely what his role in Potocari was. I knew he was a member of the special brigade of the ministry of internal affairs, but I didn't know specifically what his role was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the special brigade of the MUP, is that the same organisation that Mr. Borovcanin was a member of that you had spoken of earlier?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, did you know the hierarchy between Mr. Jevic and Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, roughly, yes. I was aware of it. I knew that Mr. Borovcanin was Mr. Jevic's superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone else around the Hotel Fontana at this time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in the area outside the hotel, I noticed myself Petar Uscumlic and Mr. Josipovic. I also noticed members of DutchBat who after the meeting were on their way back to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any discussions between you and the DutchBat people?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after they returned, they asked me what the plan was for later concerning the buses, the evacuation and so on and so forth. I told them that preparations were underway and that the buses would soon be there. I told them they should go back to their base in Potocari to wait for the evacuation to start.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall which members of DutchBat you said this to?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember specifically Mr. Rutten because I knew him personally, and I had been in touch with him countless times before. I don't remember specifically who the other officer was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after speaking to these Dutch officers?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, I went to Potocari. Actually, I stayed for a while outside the hotel, and then I left for Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stop by your command post before going to Potocari, the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not then. I didn't go to the command post of the Bratunac Brigade because it was on a different road. I went straight to Potocari from the hotel, from outside the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before going to Potocari, did you communicate with your commander Mr. Blagojevic about anything?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not on that day. On that day I didn't communicate with him. I didn't talk to him on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak with him later that day?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask that he stop leading the witness. The witness indicated and I quote: "He says on that day I didn't communicate with him. I didn't talk with him on that day." And then the question is: "Did you speak with him later that day?" It's a suggestive question. Now, if Mr. McCloskey wishes to refresh the memory or to impeach his own witness, I have no objection to that. But as it's phrased, it's leading in nature. I appreciate the difficulties the gentleman is having at the time. This is a very key witness, it's a delicate issue, and I just want to go by the numbers on this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that the witness has already answered that question. He said: "Not on that day." Mr. McCloskey, if you have some evidence that the witness had the opportunity to speak to Mr. Blagojevic, just show it to him. Otherwise, I'm afraid that you have to drop this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's not a leading question, I don't believe, is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, I don't think it's a leading question. But the answer is quite obvious from this witness. He said: "Not on that day. On that day, I did not communicate with him. I did not talk to him on that day." I think that's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, I can try to get to this question, Your Honour. But I'll go on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may be allowed to clarify this, I think there has been a misunderstanding. My understanding of Mr. McCloskey's question was about that day before I left for Potocari, whether I saw the commander. That's how I understood the question. And my answer was that on that day, I meant that specific time of day before I left for Potocari, I did not see Commander Blagojevic. I abide by that. However, on the 12th, on that same day, I did, in fact, see Mr. Blagojevic, but not before I had left for Potocari. That's my final answer to this question. I think I failed to understand Mr. McCloskey's question clearly enough, so I can only offer my apologies with this correction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you speak or communicate with Commander Blagojevic before going to carry out these duties in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason was simple. I've already referred to my conversation with Colonel Jankovic. Colonel Jankovic, among other things, told me that the units that I was to coordinate in Srebrenica had been issued orders and that the units that would take part in that operation were already in Potocari. I believed, as seen perfectly normal, that the commanders had already assigned units and planned all activities related to the evacuation. I thought my role in the whole thing was clear. That's why I didn't deem it necessary to go back to the commander to ask for more orders and more instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So about what time did you get to Potocari that day?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, about 1.00, perhaps a little later, between 1.00 and 2.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the units that were present in Potocari at the time you got there.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. What I can state with certainty is that I saw police units there and units of the army of Republika Srpska. As for the police units I saw, I saw units under the command of Mr. Jevic. Those were units of the special brigade of the MUP. Further, I saw members of the public security station in Bratunac whose chief was Josip Bratunovic. I also recognised members of the police with German shepherds. I also saw people from the corps police. I saw people from the 10th reconnaissance and sabotage detachment as well as members of the Drina Wolves from the Zvornik Brigade. I also saw members of the Bratunac military police. I saw members of our 2nd and 3rd Bratunac infantry battalions. Those roughly speaking were the units that were present in the area. I may have missed out on one or two of the units, but those units were certainly there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The units of the 10th reconnaissance and sabotage detachment, where are they from?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 10th reconnaissance and sabotage detachment was attached to the main staff. I know that. They were directly under the command of the main staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the record says "Bratunac military police." Is that Bratunac Brigade military police?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's who I had in mind, the Bratunac Brigade military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall any other military police units that were present in Potocari there?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, there were members of the corps police in Potocari, members of the police battalion from the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And any other units that you recall from the main staff besides the 10th sabotage detachment?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. There were also some members of the 65th Protection Regiment also attached to the main staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just briefly describe the scene in Potocari when you arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That day in Potocari, there were in my assessment between 25 and 30 thousand people in a very small area. They were put up in various compounds belonging to companies. It's an industrial area, mainly in the village of Potocari itself. The situation was very difficult. It was horrendous. There were many people there who were exhausted. They looked bad. There were many sick people there, many children, elderly people. There was chaos there. They were scared. The situation was very difficult among those people there who were awaiting transport.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you carry out the instructions that you'd heard from Kosoric, Popovic, and Colonel Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did exactly what I had been ordered to do, exactly in the way in which I was issued instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber what you did.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the first buses arrived, or rather just before, I got in touch with Mr. Jevic. I told him how the evacuation should be conducted and what his role was in connection with the buses, organising those buses, and other issues related to the transport of the civilian population. Then I gave instructions to units who were separating the men from the rest. I gave them instructions to separate all military-aged men in Potocari, and I showed them the house in which these men were to be temporarily detained. After that, I said the men would be taken to other facilities that were assigned for their temporary detention. As for that particular aspect, I was the direct coordinator for those units who were busy separating and detaining the men and evacuating the civilians towards Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which units actually took part in the physical separation of the men from their families?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th, the units taking part were both the police units, the unit with German shepherds. Police units from the Drina Corps also took part. Elements of the 10th sabotage detachment also took part, soldiers from the 65th Protection Regiment, as well as elements of the Bratunac Brigade police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many members of the Bratunac Brigade military police platoon were present in Potocari taking part in these events?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on my knowledge, there would have been between 10 and 15 people, 15 maximum, from the Bratunac Brigade in the area at that time. That was as many as they could afford to second to us in addition to their normal day-to-day tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the ranking soldier present from the Bratunac Brigade military police?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Srebrenica -- I'm sorry, in Potocari, Mirko Jankovic was present. He would come occasionally. He was the commander of the military police platoon of the Bratunac Brigade. As far as ranks or other officers from the Bratunac Brigade were concerned, I don't think there was anyone else in the platoon. He was, I believe, a lance corporal or a senior corporal, something like that. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The infantry battalions from the Bratunac Brigade that you described, what were they doing in Potocari on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: To the mischaracterisation. The gentleman indicated "units" not battalions. In his previous answer, he indicated that he saw members of the Bratunac Brigade, and then he characterised them as units. The question by the Prosecution was battalions. So that's a mischaracterisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, according to my records, the witness testified the 2nd and 3rd battalions of that brigade was present. I mean, that is from his previous answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right, Your Honour, that they were from battalions, but the question, the way it was phrased, it was as if the entire battalion was there. As I understand his testimony from earlier, it was -- he said units, unless I wasn't listening correctly and until there's a clarification by the witness that the entire battalion was there, the 2nd and 3nd battalion were in Potocari on that particular morning. But it's my impression that he said units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think it's a big issue. But anyway, Mr. McCloskey, you may ask some questions to clarify this issue before we have the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, there's -- I have made no suggestion that the entire battalions were there, and I think that was clear from the questioning. But I will -- thank you. I'll...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I clarify this matter. I said that in addition to the units that I've enumerated, present in Potocari were also elements of the 2nd and 3nd infantry battalions of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. I apologise. I will try to be very specific and precise when answering questions. I can also add that present there were also elements of the 2nd and 3nd infantry battalions from the 1st Light Infantry Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps one last question before the break. What were the elements of these battalions doing in Potocari on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Elements of those battalions mostly helped with the evacuation. They secured the area in Potocari, the area in which the civilian population was being held, and they helped with the evacuation and transfer, rather, deportation of Muslims from Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It looks like it's about break time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have 40 minutes break. We'll resume at 10 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, we are in Potocari on the afternoon of 12 July. Can you give us another example of how you coordinated the activities that were going on.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, Mr. McCloskey. I could give you endless examples, but I'll mention one. When the evacuation started, or rather, the transport of women and children, some problems arose in connection with the buses and establishing some sort of order with them. And Mr. Jevic was in charge of this part of the operation. After I had noticed this problem, I ordered Jevic to change the place where the buses were turning around, and that is what he did. He relocated this, or rather, he moved this position some 100 or 200 metres towards the UNPROFOR compound where there was an expansion so that the buses could make their about turn and the column could be formed under more normal conditions. There were other examples, too. For example, at the spot where the men were separated from their families, I suggested to the soldiers that they take care and make sure that they would let pass as many civilians as a bus could take so as not to cause a chaotic situation. That is, not to allow more civilians to come out than could be boarded onto the buses and trucks. I suggested that they acted in that way, and they followed my instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What senior officers did you see in Potocari that day, the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day in Potocari, I saw first of all General Mladic. Then I also saw General Krstic. I saw Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic. I saw Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric. I also saw Major Dragoslav Trisic from the Bratunac Brigade. Lieutenant-Colonel Krsmanovic, Colonel Acamovic. From the police, I already said I saw and coordinated with Dusko Jevic, and I could say that there were many officers present in Potocari on that day. And I have listed those that I actually saw and can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I saw him on the 12th or the 13th, and I'm really unable to confirm that. I did see him in Potocari, but I'm not sure that that was -- actually, I did see him on both days, but I had no communication with him on either of those days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Blagojevic in Potocari on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. McCloskey, I did not see Colonel Blagojevic in Potocari on the 12th myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him on the 13th of July in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see Colonel Blagojevic in Potocari on either day myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you saw Major Trisic. Can you remind the Court who this is and, if you know, what he was doing?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Major and reserve Dragoslav Trisic was the assistant commander of the Bratunac Brigade for the logistics. And what I know for certain is that Major Dragoslav Trisic was also engaged as a member of the team for organising transportation and evacuation of civilians from Potocari. I forgot to mention and wish to add that in Potocari, I also saw officers from the Bratunac Brigade, from the logistics department, Captain Milosavljevic, and corporal or senior corporal Mr. Stevic, and Mr. Pavle Loncarevic. All these officers were from the logistics organ of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Acamovic, what was he doing -- what was he and what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Acamovic was the assistant commander for logistics in the Drina Corps. And he was assigned, and I know that to be in charge of the overall organisation of the transportation, the provision of trucks and buses for logistic support in the sense of the provision of fuel, the distribution of personnel, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how about Mr. Krsmanovic who you also just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mentioned Lieutenant-Colonel Krsmanovic. Mr. Krsmanovic is an officer from the logistics organ of the Drina Corps. He is an officer in that body, and he feels engaged to be chief of the transportation service and the immediate superior was Acamovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you communicate that day, the 12th, with Colonel Acamovic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th, I did not communicate with Colonel Acamovic because I had no need to contact him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about Lieutenant-Colonel Krsmanovic, did you communicate with him on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this process of evacuation of the women and children and the separation and detention of the men, did you see any of the Muslims abused by Serb soldiers or police?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey. At the very spot where the separation was taking place of the men from their families, I saw innumerable cases of abuse and mistreatment of the men being separated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind? What kind of abuse during the separation did you see? Can you describe it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. After the separation, which was done in a rough and inappropriate way, personal belongings were seized and thrown onto a pile which was formed on the way to the White House where they were taken. Then there was physical abuse and beating of those men with hands and feet. Then there was verbal abuse; that is, they were called balijas and Turks and Ustashas and the like. Then those who passed through this point were turned back from the buses they had reached and separated and told to go back to the place where the already separated men were temporarily detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any superior officers of the MUP or superior officers of the VRS forces ever attempt in any way to stop this abuse?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. While I was present there, during the separation and this mistreatment, I didn't see any of the immediate officers in command trying to prevent the mistreatment of these men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself do anything to try to stop this?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't do anything. I didn't try to prevent the mistreatment or the abuse of those men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a dereliction of your responsibility as a military officer?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one can say that though I was aware and an eyewitness of what was going on, I didn't undertake anything myself personally, nor did I insist that such measures be taken by the officers in charge of units that I was coordinating. And I do think that it was a dereliction of my duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think your failure to prevent these abuses encouraged the abuses in any way?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. I think that my behaviour also contributed to the abuse continuing throughout the period of evacuation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain that, why junior soldiers might feel encouraged when their seniors are not preventing them from such abuse?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Calls for speculation, Your Honour. He can describe exactly what he in particular did to encourage. As I understand, he participated in some of the abuses over there, so he can give that description. So maybe then, there may be a follow-up question. But the way it's stated, given the lack of foundation, he's asking the witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, it is a speculation because he could not say why the junior officers did that. You may rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact that your seniors had issued orders of the nature that you've described, separating Muslim men to be killed, and the fact that senior officers were present during this abuse, did that encourage you in any way to continue this dereliction of your duties?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is a military officer supposed to lead by example?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do the junior troops look to their officers on how to properly conduct themselves?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Should they have?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you in Potocari on the 12th before you left the area?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of that day I spent in Potocari; that is, the day of the 12th. Once I arrived at Potocari, I stayed there. I stayed there until the last convoy arrived. That is when men started to board the means of transport, those that were separated for evacuation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do at this point during the last part of the day in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, I went to the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about what time did you arrive to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, shall we say between 20 and 2100 hours, roughly, around that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, after my involvement in Potocari, I informed the Bratunac Brigade commander of my activities during that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you and the commander when you informed him of your activities of the day?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally informed the brigade commander in his office at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anybody else in the office with you and your commander at this time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the two of us were alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you outline for us what you had told your commander about your activities that day.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told him everything that had happened on that day, the 12th, and what I had been involved in. I told him about the orders I had received. Then I told him that I was engaged in Potocari. I told him what my duties were there. I told him how the evacuation evolved and what my main tasks were. I told him about certain details regarding the separation of those men in Potocari and the deportation, or rather, detention first in the White House and then in the Vuk Karadzic elementary school. I told him that I had information that those men would later be killed. I didn't tell him who my source was, who had told me that. And that would be in brief the contents of the information I passed on to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if anything, did Mr. Blagojevic say to you as you were explaining him these events?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing special. He didn't say anything in particular. When I was reporting to him about the situation in Potocari, I told him that the situation was extremely difficult, that there were many problems, that it was all dreadful. His reaction was nothing in particular. He just said that he was aware that that was so and that he had no special opinion about it, that those were the orders and that what was being done was what had been ordered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you take him to mean when he said to you that he was aware that "that was so" and that "those were the orders"?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just say what my impression was at the time, and that was that this operation which was being implemented, that he had been informed about it, that he was well aware of it, and that what I told him was nothing new to him and that these were not new information that he was hearing for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he do anything to dissuade you from carrying out future conduct in relation to the separation and murder of the men?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't receive any instructions or any orders of any kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he do anything to dissuade you from taking part in the organisation of the transportation of the women and children from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he do anything to encourage your continued involvement in these events that evening? Did he say or do anything that evening to encourage your continued involvement in this operation to move out the women and children and detain and kill the men?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't say anything along those lines that would give me the impression that he was encouraging me to do anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he -- what was your understanding of what your duties would be the following day, 13 July, based on your meeting with your commander?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding was that the following day, I would continue to be engaged in that operation until its completion, that is, the evacuation, separation, and detention of the separated men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did your commander ever say anything that night suggesting that you would continue those duties the next day?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That night or rather that evening he didn't, but the next day he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So how long do you think you were in the office talking to your commander about the day's events that evening?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that conversation didn't last long. Shall we say between 15 and 20 minutes, very roughly speaking, and a maximum of that amount of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that meeting, I went to my own office and wrote a report to the corps command, to the department for intelligence and security affairs, regarding the situation and the progress of the evacuation during that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any significant details in that written report that you didn't -- or that you hadn't discussed with your commander in your previous meeting with the commander?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was nothing in particular except, I wish to point out, that in that report I didn't indicate the intention to kill. I wrote down all the other information I had in that report to the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do with that written report?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That report I took to the communications centre where there is a code. I handed it to the person who actually dispatches such reports, and that evening he sent that report to the corps command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you deliver the written report to anyone else personally?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That report does not -- is not as a rule handed to anyone else. That was the normal practice. After the exchange of information, I wrote down what I had informed the commander of, and there was no need for me to carry that report to anyone, and not even to the commander for his inspection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any other dealings with any other officers at the Bratunac Brigade that evening?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. At the Bratunac Brigade headquarters on the 12th in the evening, I talked to -- but this was not in the form of an official conversation, in the operations room, I spoke to a group of officers who happened to be there that evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who do you recall were there in that group?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the presence of the assistant commander for logistics, Dragoslav Trisic. I think, but I'm not sure, that also present were his associates from the transportation service and the technical service. I think that an officer from the operations and training sector was there, Milorad Micic, I think. Anyway, officers from the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this informal meeting as you've called it, did that occur before or after your meeting with Mr. Blagojevic in his office?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, this was no meeting. I just came there. After sending the report, I came to the operations room. It was just an informal contacts with those people because that was our regular habit, to gather there after the day's activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you discuss of significance?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We mostly discussed the situation as it was in Potocari. Each one of us briefly expressed his views and impressions of what he had seen during the day. So we discussed this difficult situation, the evacuation, and everything that they had seen and I had seen in Potocari. We did not discuss the question of killing, and I didn't discuss that matter with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a particular assignment that evening in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 12th of July, 1995, I was the duty officer in the command of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And briefly describe to us what the duties of the duty -- brigade duty officer were at that time in your brigade.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duties of the duty officer in the brigade are mostly to sit there, to be on duty in a room that is known as the operations room. Also, the duty of the officer on duty is all the information received from a superior command and all requests or needs coming from subordinate units of the battalion, to receive them in that operations room, to record them, and the information that he considers to be urgent or are marked as urgent, that about them he should inform the chief of staff or the commander. Also, the duty of the duty officer is to record all information as he receives them regarding the movement of enemy forces or intelligence information, regardless of the level they may be coming from, which means from both subordinate units and superior commands, from neighbouring units.
