And in a timely fashion and fully, to inform the chief of staff or the commander of the brigade of the same. And also, as is quite normal, to control and take all measures to provide security for the headquarters and all the other tasks that may be assigned to him, aside from his regular duties by the chief of staff or the commander and to carry them out. And of course, this also implies passing on orders from superior units to subordinate units when they go through the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the working hours of the duty officer that night?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, to all intents and purposes, the duty officer would stay on duty by 12.00 insofar as I can remember, and at 12.00, he would be relieved by the assistant duty officer in the brigade. That was the principle. However, as on that day I had been busy with the activities in Potocari, I was being replaced by staff officers. And that night, I stayed until 3.00 in the morning at the brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say normally, the duty is to 12.00, is that 12.00 noon or 12.00 midnight?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2400 hours, midnight. That's what I mean. 12.00 in the evening, midnight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so why did you stay until 3.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed until 3.00 a.m. Because during that day, I had not been in the operations room for the most part. I spent most of the day back in Potocari. But I remember most clearly is the reason my assistant was standing in for me most of that time. When I arrived in the operations room, he left to rest and relieve me later on as the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was this person that relieved you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That evening, Mirko Jankovic stood in for me. He was the commander of the military police platoon in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who the duty officer was during the day when Mirko Jankovic was in Potocari and you were also in Potocari, as you've described earlier?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all I can tell you is that this was the established practise. If the duty officer needed -- for example, this did happen to me a number of times before this day we're talking about. In that case, the clerks, for example, Milorad Micic was an administrator in the operations and training department who would very often relieve operations duty officers because he was physically there, and he had the spare time to do it. And he would often stand in for me and for other people, too. I don't remember exactly who replaced me on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may object here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would ask if you could please caution the witness to answer the question and only the question. He was asked a particular question, and then it was a non sequitur that has nothing to do with the question he was being asked. And if he wishes to volunteer information, or if he needs to explain an answer, he can ask permission or he can just do so, as is the habit in the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think the witness answered the question by his last sentence. Of course, the witness has to understand that this is a question/answer process. If the Prosecution need more informations, he could ask you about those informations. Just concentrate on the questions the Prosecution asks to you. Do you understand? Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do at 3.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At 3.00 a.m., I went back home to sleep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you next continue your duties as an officer of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I continued my duties on the 13th, in the morning. Just after 7.00, I arrived at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do that morning at the brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That morning, I spent some time in the operations room after which I spoke to Commander Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before speaking to your commander, did you receive any intelligence information about the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 12th in the evening, and on the 13th in the morning, I was receiving intelligence on the position and movement of the Muslim column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What information did you get about the Muslims on the morning of the 13th in the direction of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received information that they were moving towards Konjevic Polje, that already at that time in the morning hours, Muslims had been captured there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you went to see your commander, was there anybody else in the room with you and he?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, there was no one else, just the two of us alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say to you, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me to continue my activities, the ones that I'd started on the 12th, that I should get involved on the same tasks and assignments that I had been involved in on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he mention any of those things specifically, any of the specific tasks?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same tasks as the previous day. The evacuation of the civilian population, the women and children, the separation of men, and the coordination of work in the Potocari area where forces were active as on the previous day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you make any reports to him, or any statements?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aside from the information that was related to the movement of Muslims and their column, we also knew that men were beginning to be captured on that road, on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell your commander that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any comment about that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing special.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so what did you do after that -- let me ask. Was there anybody else present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It has been asked and answered. The answer was no, nobody was present in the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, you are too fast. Well, Mr. McCloskey, maybe you could reconsider your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wasn't sure I had asked if. I just wanted to make sure it was clear. If Mr. Karnavas tells me I did, I believe him, and we can go on to another question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may continue your question to make sure that question is answered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just -- just to make sure, was there anybody in the room when you had this meeting with your commander on the morning of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I have said before, no one else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that meeting, I went to Potocari. In Potocari, I found units that were already active there. That day, like the previous day, I worked on coordination, on providing assistance, providing advice related to the continuing evacuation, to the separation of men, to the temporary detention of men, and the transfer of men to a temporary detention facilities in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you there on this visit to Potocari on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Potocari only very briefly on the 13th. So on the whole, this lasted for one hour at most, perhaps a little longer after which I went back to the headquarters, or rather, to the military police building where the military police were stationed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in Potocari on the 13th, did you see any abuse of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw the same thing that had happened on the previous day, on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslim men or women or children murdered by anyone in Potocari on the 12th or 13th?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Neither on the 12th, nor on the 13th did I see anyone killed. However, I did hear that these things had happened outside the base where the civilian population was gathered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you get this information from, that someone -- or that Muslims had been killed outside the base?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard this from the DutchBat people, and also from some soldiers who were in Potocari, or rather, from the policemen who were in Potocari, policemen from the Bratunac security station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say "policemen from the Bratunac security station," you're talking about MUP, Ministry of the Interior police forces?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those were members of the ministry of internal affairs from the Bratunac public security station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 12 or 13th, was there any gunfire in and around Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was gunfire on both days, both in and around Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do when you went back -- you said you went back to the Bratunac Brigade command. I believe you went to the offices of the military police. What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I arrived at the military police building, I found out that during that day, General Mladic was supposed to pass down the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje Road along with a group of officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you find this out from?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duty operations officer of the military police told me. So did the commander of military police, Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So does the military police platoon have its own separate duty officer as from the brigade duty officer?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to its structure, a military police platoon had a duty operations officer within the military police platoon on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we'll have an exhibit later on, an aerial image. But can you just tell us briefly where the military police offices are compared with the Bratunac Brigade headquarters offices.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. The Bratunac Brigade headquarters was at the Kalin factory in Bratunac. In front of that building, there was another prefab building at a distance of about 20 or 30 metres from the brigade headquarters. This building was not physically linked to the headquarters, but it was in the immediate vicinity. Like I said, nothing special, two buildings. One was the brigade headquarters, and the other was the police building nearby. That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do with this information about Mladic going in that area, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, I took a vehicle and a police officer with me, and I drove out on to the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje Road. I wanted to check whether the road was safe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About what time did you leave Bratunac and drive along the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje Road?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be very specific about this, but it may have been about 11.00, perhaps half past 11.00. Maybe even a little later, but it was around that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see along that road?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the way down that road as far as Kravica, I didn't see anything out of the ordinary. Near Kravica, in the Sandici area, I saw forces of the special brigade of the MUP. In Sandici, I saw heavy weaponry, Pragas, self-propelled machine-guns, tanks that I knew belonged to the MUP special brigade. Further, I saw forces deployed between Sandici all the way to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who was in command, immediate command of these forces stationed along this road, these MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that those were forces under the command of Ljubisa Borovcanin. The immediate commander was Dusko Jevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see any Muslims along that road at that time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw several captured Muslims as I was passing on my way to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall roughly the area that you saw the captured Muslims and roughly how many?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was passing, I saw them in the Sandici area. There must have been between 10 and 15 men who had been captured, perhaps even less than that, but roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you met with Dusko Jevic in the morning of the 13th during your visit to Potocari that morning?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the morning on the 13th, I met Dusko Jevic in Potocari. In addition to the instructions to continue with the same tasks as on the previous day, I also told Dusko Jevic to convey the order to his units along the road that the captured Muslims should be assembled in one place, that they should be secured, and that they would later be evacuated to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you referring to Muslims captured along the Konjevic Polje/Bratunac Road?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So back on your trip along that road, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question. I don't think I understood the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just going back to your trip along the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje Road, where did you end up driving to and stopping?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came from the direction of Kravica and stopped at the junction in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see there at this junction? Can you just describe for us what this junction looks like and who, if anyone, you saw.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The junction is a crossroads mainly. There's a road coming from -- turning off right to Kaznemik [phoen], and then to the right there's a road leading to Nova Kasaba and Vlasenica. It was there I found members of the MUP from the Bratunac public security station. There were a large number, or rather many Muslims there who had been captured and detained in a house guarded by men from the engineering battalion from Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what the engineering battalion is, who it belonged to, what kind of facility was there.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The engineering battalion was part of the Drina Corps. The battalion was based in some privately owned houses in Konjevic Polje. That's where the headquarters was, their communication centre, the kitchen, and other facilities. I think partly they were using the elementary school in Konjevic Polje, the elementary school building to accommodate their people and provide logistics for them. All in all, this is a unit which before combat operations had already been stationed in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned you'd seen large numbers of Muslim prisoners in this area. Can you give us any kind of an estimate of roughly the amount you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that area, according to my rough estimate, there were between 200 and 250 Muslims who had been captured. If you count in all the captured persons who were in a meadow in Konjevic Polje, those detained in one of the buildings across the road from the junction itself, an old building, and some of the captured men who were put up in a house used by members of the engineering battalion, that would have been the total number of people captured in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a gas station today in Konjevic Polje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is one. The gas station is where the old building was, the one that I have been talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This old building is one of the buildings where the Muslim prisoners were stored?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do when you got to this area and you saw this?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to the MUP people who were manning the checkpoint there. I told them to assemble all the Muslims that had been captured and detain them in those buildings. I said that transport would be organised and provided for those Muslims in the course of the day, and they would eventually be transferred to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there some kind of a MUP headquarters building in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had a permanent checkpoint there. I do know that in that period of time, a unit from the special brigade was housed there in the premises of the elementary school in Konjevic Polje, whereas the command in Konjevic Polje, the only command or headquarters, was of the engineers' battalion which had its headquarters in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after informing the MUP officers there of what to do with captured prisoners, what else did you do?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, I waited for General Mladic to arrive, and it had been announced that he would be passing through Konjevic Polje. In the meantime, I was informed by members of the MUP that an important prisoner was being held in a house, and his name is Resid Sinanovic, and he was important because he was on the list of war criminals, former head of the public security station in Bratunac, or the MUP in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do in relation to Resid Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to Resid Sinanovic, when I left for Bratunac, I personally took Resid Sinanovic with me in the car and drove him to the police of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did that because I was told that he was among the people who were war criminals and that he was responsible for certain acts or military activities that had taken place in Bratunac Municipality. And I simply thought that as such, he needed to be taken and handed over to the police, interrogated regarding those events because in that period of time, there was certain killings and murders among the Serb population, military men and civilians, that had not been fully investigated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who in particular do you recall did you turn him over to at the military police?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took Sinanovic over myself, drove him to Bratunac, and turned him over to Zlatan Celanovic, a graduate lawyer who was a member of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this lawyer, Mr. Zlatan, is his first name, was he associated with the military police in some way?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Celanovic, Zlatan, in practise had a role and position in the military police platoon. And throughout that period, even though in paper and according to orders he had different duties by establishment, he was engaged throughout until the end of the war in the military police building, and he engaged in activities that mostly were related to the military police and had to do with legal matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever interview and interrogate prisoners to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Zlatan Celanovic did interview prisoners, compile reports, and a copy of those reports would also be sent to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just take you back to Konjevic Polje. Before you take Mr. Sinanovic to Bratunac, what do you do there at Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Konjevic Polje, I gave instructions to the officers of the MUP and the units engaged there as to how prisoners should be treated after being captured. I waited in Konjevic Polje for the arrival of General Mladic. In Konjevic Polje, I reported to him. I saw him address the captives in Konjevic Polje. And after he left, I returned to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What instructions did you give the MUP on how to deal with the prisoners that they had in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told members of the MUP that the prisoners in Konjevic Polje: Those that surrender or those that are captured should be detained in premises that can easily be secured, that during the day transportation would be organised, and that those imprisoned Muslims would be transported to Bratunac during the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your knowledge, what was going to happen to those prisoners that went from the Konjevic Polje area to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same that was to happen, or rather, what had been planned and ordered regarding prisoners in Potocari. And in my opinion, all those captured in that period enjoyed the same status, whether it was on the roads or in Potocari itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that status?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those prisoners were to be transported to Bratunac, temporarily detained in premises and buildings designated for that temporary detention, and after that, killed like all the others that had been separated on the 12th and 13th in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had any officer or superior specifically told you that regarding the fate of the Muslim men along the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje Road?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can do is describe to you my encounter with General Mladic and his gesture when I reported to him regarding the prisoners. He addressed the prisoners and said to those in the meadow not to worry at all, that transportation would be organised, that they would be transferred to free territory. That was what he said when he addressed them. When he completed that speech, in the middle of the road where I had reported to him, I asked him: "General, sir, what is going to happen to these men?" And he simply gestured. He didn't say anything. With his hand in answer to my question, he waved his hand and showed me what would happen. I understood that to mean that those men would be killed. Actually, I saw that to be a confirmation of what was already happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may interrupt, I notice that the witness made a gesture. I don't know if that was the gesture that General Mladic made, but he did make a gesture, and it wasn't recorded on the record. Perhaps Mr. McCloskey could clarify that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe Mr. McCloskey will ask a few questions along this line. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can the record reflect that the witness made a gesture with his hand across his chest area with his palm down, just a sweeping gesture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to this gesture from General Mladic, what did you think was going to happen to the men captured along the Konjevic Polje/Bratunac Road on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any thoughts about it. I knew what was going to happen to them, Mr. Prosecutor. I knew that those men would be captured, and after that killed. I knew that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you base that knowledge on, if you could just briefly tell us?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That knowledge of mine was based, first of all, on the conversation I had had with Mr. Popovic and Mr. Kosoric. They personally told me what had happened to those men. He told me what would happen to the captured Muslims. So this was all part of a unified operation, so the status of those captured along the roads did not differ in any sense from those in Potocari. Those captured along the roads were able-bodied men. In Potocari, there were some who were able-bodied, some who were not. And it was quite clear that if I was told that those men would be captured, temporarily detained, and after that killed, then it is quite clear that the fate of those who did not surrender and who did not come to Potocari would be exactly the same. And there was no other conclusion that I could draw except that those men would suffer the same fate as those separated in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So what did you do after dropping Resid Sinanovic off at the military police barracks?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. After you took Resid Sinanovic to the military police, what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, I, Mirko Jankovic, and Mile Petrovic, that is, the police commander and deputy police commander, from the compound of the Bratunac Brigade barracks, we took an APC which Mirko Jankovic knew how to drive, and we drove off to the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje Road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say Mirko Jankovic and Mile Petrovic, they are police commander and deputy police commander of the Bratunac Brigade military police. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I meant the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was this -- APC is an armoured personnel carrier. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was this APC from?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The armoured personnel carrier was from the Dutch Battalion, and it had been seized when the Srebrenica enclave had been captured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour was it when you were -- you and Mirko Jankovic and Petrovic were in it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a white armoured personnel carrier with the UN letters written in bold capitals, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did you go in this APC?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After we took the APC, we drove off to the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje Road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were you doing as you were driving along the road in this APC?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we moved along in this APC, Mirko Jankovic was driving. Mile Petrovic used a loudspeaker which was in the APC, and I sat on the APC. We drove from Kravica towards Konjevic Polje, and after Sandici, Mile Petrovic took the megaphone and called on the Muslims to surrender, the Muslims who were in the woods along that road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you first stop, if anywhere, along this road?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stopped for the first time somewhere in the region of the village of Pervani. I think after Sandici, there is Lolici, and then Pervani villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we stopped on that occasion, five or six Muslim soldiers surrendered to us. We took them into the APC and continued on our way to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We reached Konjevic Polje. I got off the armoured personnel carrier and told Mile Petrovic to take the prisoners to a group of other prisoners who were already there. And I went and sat down under the eaves of a house that had been burnt and where a certain number of Muslims were sitting there already, captured Muslims. I told him to take those Muslims to join that group. And after that, to come back to the spot where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After some 10 minutes or so, I heard a burst of fire not far from the spot where I was. And this burst of fire reached me from the direction of the building where the petrol station is now. This was on the bank of the River Jadar. Shortly after that burst of fire, Mile Jankovic [as interpreted] came under this awning where I was sitting and told me the following: "Chief, I've taken revenge for my brother, and I've killed them."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do upon receiving this information?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever report his killings up your chain of command?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not, Your Honours and Mr. Prosecutor. I didn't inform anyone about that killing because I felt that in view of all the numerous killings and the knowledge I had as to what would happen to all those prisoners, I didn't feel that any such report would have any sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you guys do after that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, together with Mirko Jankovic and Mile Petrovic, I returned to the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about what time did you get back to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could have been in the evening by then. So between 18 and 1900 hours. I really can't be more precise than that. But anyway, late in the afternoon, it still wasn't dark but it was the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I've just noticed -- I have been watching the monitor here. And it indicates that the gentleman might have said that it was "Mile Jankovic." We have a Mirko Jankovic and a Mile Petrovic. But it denotes that a Mile Jankovic was the one that came back and said: "Boss, I just took revenge." So if we could have some clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes we also got confused with all those names. Mr. McCloskey, you may clarify this matter for us by asking some questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it that came back and told you he'd just taken revenge upon the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mile Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you drove back to Bratunac that, as you described, late afternoon, early evening but it was still light, what did you see along the road between Konjevic Polje and Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Returning from Konjevic Polje on the way to Bratunac, I saw columns of captured Muslims moving towards Konjevic Polje. Then I also saw columns of captured Muslims moving towards Sandici, which means in the opposite direction. Then I saw again, as we moved along, some bodies next to the asphalt road. There would be groups of two, three, four, or five bodies, depending. Then in Sandici, I saw a large group of captured Muslims in a meadow in Sandici. And in Sandici, I recognised and identified the same combat vehicles that I had seen on my way to Konjevic Polje, which means a Praga, self-propelled machine-gun, and tanks. And after that, in the Kravica area, I saw several soldiers, but nothing in particular. In Kravica, I also saw members of the Bratunac MUP on my way back, and they were standing in front of the old cultural centre which had been burnt and destroyed. And after Kravica, I didn't see anything special. I continued on my way to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslim prisoners alive or dead around the area of the Kravica warehouse as you went by it that afternoon/evening?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I already said that in -- on that part of the road, I didn't see any prisoners in the area of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your trip from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje and back, the second one you've just now described, aside from yourself, Mirko Jankovic, and Mile Petrovic, did you see any members of the Bratunac Brigade along that road?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was there, I didn't see members of the Bratunac Brigade along the road. I saw members of other military units. There were troops, but I really was not able to tell which units they belonged to because the uniforms of civilians and policemen are almost identical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to recognise by name any of the MUP officers that you saw in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Konjevic Polje, I did recognise members of the MUP from Bratunac. There was Nenad Deronjic, a policeman. And another policeman, Mirko -- I know his name, but I can't remember the surname. Mirko Peric. So one was an older policeman, and this Deronjic was a younger policeman. And they were in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your first trip to Konjevic Polje where you picked up Resid Sinanovic, did you see any Bratunac Brigade soldiers or officers along that road or in that area?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I really didn't identify or see any members of the Bratunac Brigade along that road that I was moving on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a subject you briefly mentioned, the uniforms of the special brigade of the MUP under Borovcanin and Jeftic, was there any way to distinguish those uniforms from the uniforms of VRS soldiers such as the Bratunac Brigade or other VRS soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, you could only tell by the insignia that the special brigade wore on their sleeves, the sleeves of their uniforms. That emblem and insignia differed, and you could identify them by those insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this might be a good place to stop for the day. I think we're about through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Could I ask you at this moment how long, how many hours, are you going to use for tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'll take a look at my outline. One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I hope to finish tomorrow. It's hard to gauge precisely, but I only have two pages of the outline. I have some documents and a couple of intercepts to go over. But I don't think that there should be any lengthy discussion on any of those. I am very much going to try to finish up tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's very encouraging. And we lost some time. For instance, last week we lost two days. And today we lost one sitting. And if you need some time longer, we might sit tomorrow afternoon. But we hope we will not. Well, tomorrow morning, we'll go back to Courtroom III upstairs. So we'll resume at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 1.36 p.m. To be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of September, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
